app: 11. ADHD Habit Tracker, To Do List - Daily Planner, Schedule Tasks
text:
ADHD Friendly . Having ADHD is not a constant and for everybody the experience is different. But there are some unifying elements that I think most people who suffer from ADHD can agree upon and that is time managment and not only making goals for yourself but actually remembering both to attend to them and that you set them in the first place.

This is where timecap becomes extremely useful, it wont solve the problem but it will definitely help. It keeps me focused and on track. It's like a butler just making sure I remember what those goals were, and doesn't reprimand me if I fail or forget. 

I would like a bit more dicipline from it though since it doesn't seem to notify me when I'm forgetting, but that might be a failure on my part and not knowing how to make it do exactly that. It's only an app and not my own personal Alfred.

I'd recommend it though to anyone that wants to get a better overview of how they want to spend their time and especially if you are like me, have trouble sticking to your goals and/or remembering them. I'd like to add that I'm using the premium version but I'm also all for paying for stuff that works.

It won't transform your life but it can 100% help, if you use it correctly. Either way the responsability always ends with you.

I recommend Alarmy to anyone interested in an alarm app, and especially to any of those people who are neurodivergent like me.

app: 46. everyday - Habit Tracker - Daily Routine Checklist
text:
Visually compelling and wonderfully executed . I’ve tried numerous habit trackers and reminder apps over the years, and nothing has grabbed me so completely as this one. The visuals, the clean interface, the gentle reminders to not skip two days (but no “punishment” other than a break in the color gradient if you need to skip twice), the incredibly compelling and nuanced widget options— all of this earns a “wow” from me. I’m historically resistant to subscriptions, but $29/year for what this app is giving me in terms of mental health is an absolute steal. 

Yes, you could do this on paper, but will you? You could do this in a spreadsheet, but will you? Having the large widget right there on my Home Screen has been motivating in a way I have honestly never felt. If you have ADHD this is a jolt to the system in the best possible way. If you’re an artist or designer you’ll love the aesthetic. If you simply need an easy way to track a few habits, go with the free version, it’s marvelous and without ads or other shackles. If you need more than three habits, great! The paid version is well worth the subscription, and I’m glad to be putting money in a skilled independent developer’s hands. Thank you Joan!

text:
Designed to exploit, do not trust . I wish I'd read some of these other one star reviews before signing up for the subscription. I feel like an idiot for falling for it. I enjoyed the trial. I liked the application enough that I paid full price for the first month. I stopped using it, and I decided the cancel before the second month. I tried to cancel. I wasn't billed for several months - and I thought I'd cancelled it successfully, then I was hit with three bills that added up to £128.97 at once.

It feels deliberate. This was a targetted ad that I had on Instagram, and the ad specifically targetted people with ADHD. You can't just open the application and cancel it - when you open the application up, it will greet you with a quiz / features and until you navigate through before you can even get to your account settings. There's no way to close it or get at them quickly. You have to open the web page up in the browser, sign in again, and navigate through a form that is intentionally confusing / diverts your attention away with multiple screens presenting you with offers, asking why you've chosen to leave, etc. There's one in particular where you have to make a selection between to survey options to continue that is just not intuitive at all - and they all kind of look like, if you're not really paying attention, like they're confirming that you have cancelled / optional survey questions once you've completed the process. You haven't.

They say it is designed to try to hwlp structure your day but it really feels like it's designed to obfuscate as much about the app, and their other apps as possible. You can't easily flick around the features and decide which are the right ones for you. As I mentioned before, even getting to the app's main landing/home screen can take a bit of effort some days, if it decides it wants to quiz you first. app: 24. Fabulous - Daily Habit Tracker - Morning Routines & ADHD Help
text:
More difficult to navigate than it used to be . I’ve used Fabulous on and off for several years. There are things I love about it that keep me renewing the annual subscription, but the UI has changed in the last year or two and is much more difficult to navigate in my opinion.

There used to be a button in the middle labeled “make me fabulous” or something like that. It would let you choose categories like guided meditations, stretching, and the one I used the most, deep work. Now, I have no idea where to find that menu, if it’s there at all. I am only able to access the deep work feature by going through my afternoon routine since I added it there at one point.

The longest streak I ever got on my morning routine was around 70 days. I love the little pictures of the “journey” that illuminates a new area each day you continue your streak. However, that only goes for 2 or 3 weeks. It might sound silly, but seeing the next part of the picture actually really motivated me to maintain my streak.

I also realized from that longer streak that the app maybe isn’t really built for people to use long term? The daily coaching things repeated once every 3-4 weeks. The messages are always a nice reminder, but by the third time hearing the same one, I was a little disappointed there weren’t more than 20-30 in the rotation. I don’t know if that has changed by now— that streak was a couple years ago.

The one thing I love the MOST about this app is the deep work feature, specifically the long ritual to ramp up for a 4 hour deep work session. I renew every year for this alone because when I’ve tried to do the deep work ritual without the app, I don’t usually have the discipline to complete it as slowly as the app dictates. Even if I’m not planning to work for 4 full hours, I will do that ritual for any amount of deep work because it works better than anything else to get me in a productive mood. By the time I get to the end of the ritual, I am itching to start working. For someone with adhd, finding something like this that consistently works is huge. I do wish there was ambient music on the deep work feature, though, and that the app didn’t have such a tendency to crash in the middle of your 4 hour session.

text:
The most helpful app around for managing my life and my well being . UPDATED REVIEW:

Thank you, Fabulous Developers! 

High praise and kudos to you for taking all of the negative feedback and turning it around. 

The additional targeted apps, which you previously wanted me to pay a lot of extra money for, are now all included in my single existing subscription. I'm loving the Ambience app and the Enchant app so far. There are also apps focused on managing ADHD, setting goals & finding your purpose, anxiety & stress management, healthy eating, and sleep. 

One of the main reasons I stopped using the Fabulous app for the past two years, besides the obnoxious notifications, was the cumbersome and overwhelming design. For anyone who feels that life can be stressful and overwhelming – mentally, emotionally, physically – this app is for you!

Highly recommend!

Excessive money grabbing for additional apps is off putting:

This app is very helpful for routine building and growing your emotional well being. Or, it used to be. The excessive notifications put me off. There’s no middle ground, where you can choose the notifications that will be helpful, but opt out of the ones that are bothersome. The notifications are supposed to make me feel supported, but I just feel nagged. 

Also, the app now bombards me with ads and offers for their other apps. I pay for the premium membership, so I should’t be spammed by the people I’m already paying. The additional apps they want you to sign up for require a lot more money for essentially the same service. 

I’ve seen a lot of reviews about wrongful, illegal billing after customers have cancelled their subscriptions, and poor customer service when they try to get their money back. 

Be wary of signing up. But, if you can tolerate the app maker’s obnoxious money grabbing & the nuisance notifications, the app itself is great.

text:
A great tool for building habits—just wish the rewards stayed rewarding . I’ve been using Finch daily for the past 26 days, and it’s genuinely helped me stay on track with my goals. As someone with ADHD, I tend to procrastinate or avoid tasks that don’t bring immediate satisfaction, and Finch gave me that little hit of motivation I needed—at least at first.

The daily check-ins, small quests, and virtual pet rewards worked really well in the beginning. I even tried the Plus version (which I don’t mind paying for), and while it helped me collect in-app currency faster, I’ve started to feel less motivated because there’s not much I’m excited to spend it on. Most of the furniture and outfits feel repetitive—lots of similar items in different colors—and I rarely find something new or interesting for my bird. It feels like I’m seeing the same few options over and over again, which takes away from that sense of progress.

I know there’s a much bigger catalog of items that might become available in the future, but with only a handful of new items shown each day, it can feel like a long wait without much payoff.

That said, I really appreciate what Finch is doing. It’s helped me build momentum when nothing else was working. I just hope future updates make the reward system feel a bit more exciting and dynamic for long-term users.

app: 10. Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker

app: 10. Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text:

The new Supergirl adventures feel too long, require too many clicks, and include too much text. Instead of feeling supportive, they can feel overwhelming and cognitively demanding.

I am sharing this because I care about Finch and want it to succeed. But if the app continues moving in this direction, I may stop using it despite loving what Finch used to be.

text:

I have stuck with this consistently. It has helped me keep to my brain training, diet and exercise routine. It has helped improve my relationship and reduce my anxiousness. It has helped me be more productive and more focused on my work and writing. It has helped me consistently improve my mood and led to me be accepting in saying when I am happy. 

I am keen to see if the gamification continues to evolve: will there be greater customisation in the bird design, the furniture and (more importantly) the ability to add my own affirmations that appear in the cycle or that I can choose which ones to appear. I did wonder if sub-tasks would be good but I sometimes overcomplicating things actually make things worse. The design is probably aimed at a younger audience so interested to see if there is chance to see an older variation (although this feels like when books are re-published with a different cover to let adults read them without embarrassment when they should just own what they enjoy). 

I think this is worth the money and the good works that they do. I do think it is easier when you get this app with someone you know. text:
Surprisingly effective . A friend suggested this to me and I new that I’d initially enjoy it and make use of it but I thought as per usual I’d become distracted, bored and forget it existed. Surprisingly I’m quite far in now and finding it stop very useful and compelling. I have adhd and very much struggle to motivate myself to do many tasks, with a bit of setting up I’m now finding I’mactually still doing things I’d normally have given up eg eating more veg with my meals, drinking more water and such.

It works on the principle that you set yourself daily tasks which by completing you earn rainbow stones which are effectively the in game currency. You use these to buy room decorations, clothes and later on can buy other things like different colours for your finch and locations to visit. You also can connect to friends finches and send them things like hugs, compliments and so on through the day.  There’s also useful journeys which are groups of tasks that encourage you to do certain things eg feel more positive, eat more healthily and such. These contain suggested tasks but you can also add your own. 

As with anything you could frig the system if you wanted, earn lots of rainbow stones without actually doing anything but ultimately the only person you’d be cheating is yourself. The paid option goes towards keeping the app going for everyone (why I paid) and does unlock a few more slots in the randomly populated shop plus you get more seasonable achievements and some more task customisation options. However it’s very good even as a free version. There’s also an option to apply for a guardian to sponsor you paid membership if you can’t afford it, which are generous people who pay extra per month so others can get more out of the app. There’s a few bonuses for this but nothing significant, it’s more about the desire to help other people. 

Overall this app is very much about positive mental and physical health and taking care of yourself, and you get a cute bird (and little pets for it) to help motivate you

text:
ADHD - Great at First. Loses novelty & effectiveness over time. . So I started Finch about a year ago. Anyway, so it started off great. I actually stuck with it for quite some time actually.

Which is great in the short term, but once my birb was all grown up, and I had a great about of outfits, furniture, and micropets, things kinda lost their novelty and excitement for me. 

I took a break from it for some time and gradually started logging in less and less, because it started to feel like a hassle to complete all the tasks, especially after logging in for the first time in while.

I feel like if there was a smaller task list for when we log back in after quite some time (like after 15 days or so), that might help.

I also think if there were some different activities or mini games—like some that help with memory loss and critical thinking—that’d be nice.

Also, we need a way to claim all past rewards from all the past months in the situation that you like to sit on decisions for a long time like I do.

I also want a default “claim all” rewards with a default preset that makes the selected rewards the exact same as the banner promo, as I find it difficult to make decisions, even when it comes to colors, and think it would beneficial if there was a default preset, so that everything can still look good without me making decisions.

All in all though, I think my main issue was that the novelty wore off after some time. Great app though.

text:
Massive user experience fail . I’m writing this as a psychologist who used to recommend this app to clients and as a former user who lives with PTSD, ADHD, and the impacts of a TBI. Had I known this, I would never have gotten started and would not have recommended the app. 

I spent hours of precious time and limited executive functioning to set up the app and enjoyed daily Finch fashion and nest shows with friends. I’ve not only lost almost 1500 clothing items, 1200 furniture items, numerous favorite micropets, and travel exploration progress, but also all tangible evidence of progress and friend connections. I feel like something died and I’m devastated. 

The app crashed and suddenly wanted me to create a new Finch and offered 5k rainbow stones. Having no options, no help, and 5k stones is an insulting and un-empathetic slap in the face and only adds to the devastation. I don’t have it in me to start over. 

Friends, fellow clinicians, and a user experience expert I spoke with are all shocked that an app that claims to be a mental health/self-care app would be so careless and so tone deaf re the impact of data loss. Sadly I found countless others who’ve had this experience and who’ve had no help or empathy from the Finch team. 

If clunky daily manual back ups aren’t doable for you due to the impact of TBI or mental health symptoms, then I recommend you find a different app to avoid the world of hurt I am now experiencing.

app: 10. Finch - Self-Care Pet - Daily Journal & Habit Tracker
text:
First self care app I didn’t delete! . I love this little app. It’s the first self care app I’ve ever downloaded and not deleted. I even got Finch plus and I’ve never gotten a subscription for any self-care app. There are so many pros to this app and I have been singing its praises to anyone who will listen. I only have two suggestions which could be considered cons and I’ll put those at the end but this is a  five star app.

PRO - GOALS & TO DO
The goal section of this app is honestly the shining star. It helps those of us who need it stay on track and especially those of us with ADHD who have issues with time. My favorite parts of the little to do list section & that you can have recurring goals plus you can have goals that roll over until you complete. You can have weekly goals, you can have monthly goals, and whatever else you need like one off goals such as completing your store return or what have you. Goals can also link directly to exercises if you want them to, such as stretching or gratitude jar which is one of my favorites. I have never been more on top of watering my plants until seeing it roll over every single day and realizing it’s getting closer to Friday when it was initially set. I haven’t missed any of my medicines or brushing my teeth since downloading this. It’s really great to put in two goals for medicine so I can see if I’ve taken my morning and night. It’s harder to make excuses not to do it when it rolls over, like if I don’t clean my cats water fountain today it’s just gonna be there tomorrow. Instead of having it stay dirty for two weeks.

PRO - CBT TECHNIQUES & JOURNALING
I am blown away by the sheer amount of coping mechanisms I’ve been taught by my therapist that I’ve seen pop up in Finch. You do multiple daily mood check-ins which is super important, and it tracks it and tags words you use so you can get summaries at the end of the week - such as “Mom” “Job” and “Reading” gave you the most joy and “sick” “finances” and “Suzy” were the most negative. On top of that when you do a check in and it’s negative it may prompt you to reflect on it, and it also shows the section that says “first aid.”Once you click first aid you see a lot of rescue coping mechanisms that I’ve been taught in therapy such as when you have panic attacks or when you’re feeling really down. These are exercises I’ve tried to discuss with my friends before when they’re having a hard time, and I am fully convinced that Finch worked and developed this with therapists. People put a lot of effort into this. On top of that if the going gets really tough in the top hand right hand corner of the first aid section there is helplines which is really wonderful - did you know there are specific ones such as for queer folks, trans folks, teens, warm lines when you just want someone to talk to? They also have a lot of built-in journaling, very thoughtful prompts and things to help you get in the right mindset such as gratitude jar which is one of my favorites and personal reflection questions. They even have a section on grief, and they’re all in bite-size chunks with cute little emojis. This is really what you learn in therapy if you can’t get to therapy and need something in the meantime. 

PRO - SUPER CUTE AND GRATIFYING! When you actually do your tasks you help your little Finch grow! And they’re super cute. They get stronger as you get stronger - the more you do for yourself, the more energy your Finch has to go explore and learn. You get to dress them and eventually pick colors, and you can decorate their room. 

PRO - NO ADS OR PURCHASE NECESSARY 
They don’t have pop up ads and don’t ask you to buy in game currency (it’s not really a game but you can earn and use gems on clothes and such). You don’t actually have to subscribe to get a lot out of Finch, you just can’t do yoga and a few exercises. I found that Plus is worth it when you get the $39 for a year deal. 

PRO - LONG TERM GOAL PLANS & WEEKLY REFLECTION
I like that at the end of each week they ask you what you did well and what you’d like to do better. If you select sleep better for instance, it will suggest adding certain tasks that help sleep health, such as deep breathing before bed. You can also create self care plans focusing on certain goals. The insights are great. 

CON/ SUGGESTION - LIMITED AMOUNT OF STRETCHES ETC
It’s great that there’s yoga and stretches and whatnot but there are so few stretches and exercises in some of them it’s kind of annoying as a paid user. For instance in the sleep bedtime stretches if you select lying only, there’s only 3 stretches it shows you on repeat. This applies even in the 5 and 10 minute settings which is crazy since you need plus for those. There are so many stretches out there, same with yoga and exercise, please add them! 

CON/ SUGGESTION - FINANCIAL NEED HELP
Currently, Finch has a monthly raffle for one singular month of free Finch plus for those in need, sponsored by other generous Finch users who essentially donate for this (called guardians). This is great and thoughtful but it’s luck of the draw and only one month. If you really care about providing accessible self care to anyone low income, you could do that *and* use some of the guardian money to offer a discounted rate to those in need. Such as half off after proving low income - you can link an EBT card or medicaid in other places even Amazon and Walmart Plus does it. This would allow so many more people to afford this. Or just have people write why they need it and even do it on a month by month or 3 month basis when they can reapply.

Overall, this app is wonderful. There’s so much effort put in, and if you actually try to use it to the fullest and explore all the features, you will love it. I am so glad I found it! Thank you Finch team!

text:
Beautiful, ethical and kind . The word “beautiful” is usually reserved for music, fine art, serene landscapes, aesthetically pleasing people… but it can also apply to software: Finch is beautiful.

I have been using it for 2-3 years. Although I do sometimes fall into the pit of being too ambitious and generating too many to do items for myself, Finch never says an unkind word and instead celebrates my successes — no matter how small.

But this isn’t a to-do list app: this is about self-care and compassion. It’s like a reverse tomagachi: I take care of myself, and that makes my adorable little bird grow and thrive. 

Taking care of myself might mean doing guided breathing exercises before bed (so helpful! I am glad this app got me in the habit), or stretching, or even just taking a minute to identify my current emotion, what causes it  and (optionally) journal a bit. 

Maybe the goal is simply “get out of bed” or “take a shower,” things that depression and ADHD and stress can make feel nearly impossible. And on days I can’t do that, I have reflection/journaling prompts.

If I go a few days or weeks without checking in, because life happens sometimes, Finch never guilts me about it. It welcomes me back with a cheerful wave and asks me how I feel today.

As a cynical tech nerd, I love that it keeps my data stored locally. As far as I am aware they aren’t using it for evil or profit, which is why I don’t mind paying for the app. And if you can afford it, you can pay it forward to gift a subscription to a stranger in need. There is a free version, however, which makes it accessible to all budgets.

This app was clearly made with love. If the creators ever appear at a tech conference in my area I would love to learn more about their philosophy behind it.

It’s ethical. It’s helpful. It’s kind.

And I get to dress my bird up in all manner of ridiculous outfits.

Thank you, Finch. Cheep!

Finch is different than any app I’ve ever tried to use. I have one to-do list that’s non-negociable priorities for the day. Eating. Getting sun. Changing clothes. Taking my meds. I then have a separate list that are things that improve me as a human. Doing my Spanish lessons. Loading the dishwasher. Taking my dogs on a walk. But then that list is an “only prioritize when you have the spoons to” thing which calms my completionist autistic brain. 

 I love that when you skip tasks or load them off to other days the app gives you the option to reflect on why you skipped that day. I love the affirmations and mood checkins whenever you open the app, and I love that when your mood drastically changes from one ask to the next it prompts you to write down what happened. Like yesterday I got in a spat with my husband and the app picked up I was sad. It prompted me to reflect which I did, it offered me breathing exercises afterwards which I did, AND it even prompted me to reflect on my relationship with my husband and asked questions about him which put me back in a headspace of remembering how much we love each other and that this was just a small misunderstanding. I could rave even more, but if you are struggling with any form of mental health condition or are neurodivergent in any way, DO IT. The plus version is also worth it, you’d spend at least as much as the yearly cost on planners and supplies that would inevitably get forgotten and go unused :) Just do it!

This is going to be a multi part review just because I genuinely think this app is awesome and I have so much to say.

 To start: my favorite part so far is the journeys. I LOVE being able to create my own “journey” and set / check off daily, weekly or monthly, tasks. I can’t even explain how helpful it’s already been in motivating me to get stuff done. Everything about setting and completing the goals is perfect. I love choosing an emoji for them. I love the satisfying sound it makes when you check it off, and I love that I can edit them later if I decide I want to switch them up, or one isn’t really serving me like I thought it would. 

 Secondly: I love the tracking going on in this app. It’s very satisfying and helpful to be able to see how my moods have changed from week to week/ monthly. I’m LOVING the writing element to this app and I read that that is the main science behind the mental health angle is that writing can curing. I love that I can look back at my reflections I’ve written and that they’re rated from negative to positive and I can keep track!! I am blown away by the attention to detail and I want to thank you guys for coming up with this and clearly putting so much thought and effort into it. 

 Third: I obviously love my birb. I knew I’d think they were adorable but I’m really loving all the details put into making them unique like, discovering things about them that I don’t really have control over, it makes them more authentic! Also the customizations like clothes, and how we can change color combos, over time, etc. I weirdly love how we have to unlock some features as the birb ages too, it’s just perfect.

 Lastly a note for creators: please, PLEASE continue to add new likes, dislikes, clothing, etc to this game periodically!!! It is incredible so far and I think it could go even further with the ways your birb is unique! I’d also really love to see more quizzes added. That’s the one feature that I think is super cool but maybe lacking compared to the others and it could be a really cool feature / tracker for personality tests like love languages, the meyers brigg test, and enneagram! I’ve purchased a subscription a while ago. But I didn’t end up using it much, and then I tried to figure out why as I’m always curious why my brain wants or doesn’t want to do something.
I feel like the reason is that the widget is hard to see: low contrast text on blurry background. It’s mostly those circles of different colors but the text that is barely visible for me, it doesn’t “read into brain” right away. 
So my brain is not tricked to click “done” on those circles as it takes a while to figure what exact circle i need (my vision is fine, but I do have ADHD). 
So it feels like I loose more dopamine for finding the right circle than getting a dopamine for hitting a circle as an  award for completing the habit. 
Also, I realized that habits as a list with check marks ✅ works better to motivate my brain, so I moved to a different app for now. Also, high contrast is what helps (like simple black text on white background).  
But I hope new accessibility features will be added to this one as overall it’s functionality is great.

app: 3. Inflow - Manage Your ADHD - Build focus, routine & habits
text:
Inflow is the core resource and a very powerful habit for me. . Inflow has proven to be a core resource for me as I learn to live with my ADHD. A diagnosis that continues to make me question who I am, how I got to where I am in life, and how the world works around me. Inflow’s structure with daily learning modules is steadily increasing my understanding of ADHD. It explains why I have endured such confusion and suffering throughout my life (I was diagnosed at 58!) Inflow provides me with strategies that I can actually understand, that I can logically accept and that I increasingly use in most aspects of my daily life. It hasn’t cured me (ha ha) but I do know more about why I do things the way I do. 
Amazingly I am still doing Inflow most every day, that is, for more than 2 months which is an achievement that only people with ADHD would appreciate. That’s a great achievement for me. The appbmust be structured just for us, and is rewarding enough for me to remain engaged and not to get distracted by something “shiny” elsewhere.  
The inflow app continues to be a crucial resource, for me, in my attempts to reduce the ADHD related suffering affecting me and those around me, my family and work mates .
Unexpectedly, there are other insights. For example I have also developed a degree of compassion for myself -both in the here and now, and also for myself in the past, as a child, a teenager, and throughout my adult life. I also increasingly understand why the people in my story responded the way they did. 
I strongly recommend investing in this program  to the people like myself who are genuinely confused and overwhelmed by their diagnosis that may have caused them to question everything that they thought they knew about themselves and the world around them.
In all honesty, I have to say that at first I was hesitant to start the app. Financially it was a big commitment. And would Ibstay the course?  However, based on my positive experience with the Additude website, combined with the usual overwhelming, in the moment, impulse to do the program, I swept this hesitation aside and pressed the “GET”  button. 
It costs me about about a $1 AUD a day. Much less than my mild online shopping habit and  I think it is well worth it. I do the modules-virtually every day-and has it has proved to be a rewarding and valuable part of my new routine.
Inflow has, I believe,  proven to be, for me, a significant, meaningful and positive new habit. It is a learning experience that is practical and applicable to my daily activities. It is as you might say “real world friendly” 

This is a genuine review- I am a real person. I am not being paid to write this. 

( although I wouldn’t turn down any little presents from George and the gang.)

It seemed really promising and so I didn’t cancel and ended up paying the full year subscription. It is not cheap but I felt hopeful that it would be worth it. Another selling point was that they seemed understanding of how ADHD works and committed to offering refunds anytime no questions. I wrote support to talk about getting at least a partial refund because I just wasn’t receiving any value from the app, it just wasn’t working for me. I never heard back from them.  This is a gigantic red flag and I really regret spending the money. 

I would proceed with caution before giving any money to a company as inconsistent as this one.

app: 3. Inflow - Manage Your ADHD - Build focus, routine & habits
text:
Worth every penny. . I have referred SO many of my friends to this app! 

I got curious if I had ADHD after struggling with what I call ‘chronic procrastination’. Unavoidable, crippling procrastination. Of work, of sleep, of contacting friends. 

While I was waiting for my diagnosis, I decided to try the app because if the shoe fits and it helps me, what’s the relevance of if I do or don’t have ADHD? (Spoiler: I do). 

If I could break my journey to where I am now down and how much better I can now work WITH and understand my adhd, this app contributed 70% of it. Easily.  

In the last 3 years, I’ve spent £10k on therapy and coaching from neuro divergent specialists, and that got me an extra 20% of the way. 

On reflection, it made me realise just how this app is worth every penny. 
I truly hope anyone reading this gives it a go and gets as much out of it as I have. 

One word of advice. You can lead a horse to water but you can’t force it drink. Ie. You get out of this app what you put in.
At least that’s what I found. 

All the best on your journey. It really is a gift to have adhd - even if it doesn’t always feel like it 🙏🏼

text: Fabulous help & fun! . The zoom sessions are the best! This is where myself and others with ADHD (ADHDers) rock our projects, work , etc. out.  There are 25 minutes where we focus and then a 5 or more minutes break for encouragement and sharing (no pressure to share). The moderator I am with the most is Callie, who is also an ADHDer. She has tons of experience and is extremely down to earth, motivating and helpful. She has us pace ourselves and listen to what is needed - a meal, a rest, a way to understand what is going on and helps us, etc. This is something needed b/c the executive functioning of our brains is not the same as others. There is no pressure on zoom, but there loads of great ideas. There is an electric air at times as we champion each other and when there are days when I or others of us is struggling or down, we offer each other encouragement. I have seen that this really boosts the results - it amazes me how much we all get done. The more I attend, the more I get done and live a more balanced life - it is accumulative, even though there are some up and downs. The zoom sessions are so satisfying and we also have a lot of laughs. Besides the zoom sessions, there are around 45 or so topics in mini lessons, available as well. Having an understanding of many aspects of having ADHD and ways to succeed, our strong and weak points has allowed me to move forward in my life. I was diagnosed many years ago but didn’t have the tools and knowledge. In addition to the zoom sessions and mini classes, there are questions posted to the community and it is gratifying to understand our common challenges, concerns, and wins. There are people of a wide variety of ages (many youth, I think and others, as well). I believe that if you are a student, you can get a discount. Definitely worth the try!  I have been doing this since a year ago, last July. PS I was first skeptical that the 25 minute focused sessions with 5 minutes off would work for me and felt I sure I would not like it.  I gave it a try, early on, however, and am amazed and so thankful.

text: Best Body Doubling sessions - why cancel them? . I finally found an app that works for me.. text:
If I can remember to use it, this app is amazing!!! . I don’t remember where I even heard of this app but I know I need extra support for my ADHD outside of therapy and meds. Like many, I’ve tried countless organizing apps, well being and meditation apps, etc., but none specifically tailored to, and often frustrating for an ADHD brain. I’ve only been using this app for 2 weeks and I’ve found it so helpful I’m actually writing this review!! It’s always a gamble to pay for an app but within the first 2 days I was into it, and even told my therapist about it so she could share it with other patients. 

The UI is clean and very easy to use. The steps are laid out very clearly and each day’s lesson isn’t too long or short (AND major points for the creators adding a feature to speed it up as well as rewind, and fast forward, much like a podcast. After listening to each lesson, which is spoken clearly and in a way that for the most part keeps my attention (I do often repeat the lesson recording multiple times that day), there are bullet point takeaways in text before you move on. 

If a challenge appeals to you, you don’t have to join right away, you can add them to a wishlist!!! You can also heart your favorite lessons. 

They added a medication reminder as well. I’m still exploring the app but I am just super impressed at how it has been designed to be easy for an ADHD brain to navigate. In my own opinion, the creators and developers really nailed it and I really want to say THANK YOU!!!

I’m also having my partner listen in on the lessons which have also helped him understand some of what I experience, yet have a hard time vocalizing.

text:
Good . So… For the most part, it’s well designed, mostly intuitive, thoughtful, easy to get started with lots of preset schedule ideas, how-tos, resources, and so forth. 

But the current issues I’ve been having since the latest iOS update kind of killed it for me. I’m autistic and ADHD. So while this was helpful for organizing my days, the problems just started feeling too overwhelming.

 Like the audio disruptions; clicking/sound cutting out on other apps while Me+ was open in the background. Alerts going bonkers and repeating 3, 4, 5 times or more all at once. The alarm failing to go off if Me+ wasn’t the app “currently in use.” It’s supposed to be running in the background for the alarm to work, but that stopped being enough at some point and it wasn’t going off until I was already awake (as much as an hour and 15 minutes past the alarm time) and had unlocked the phone to turn off the iOS alarm(s) and check other apps/alerts. 

It also likes to hijack the audio while the alarm is sounding, which is horrible for sensory issues first thing in the morning. Or even 4th thing… Couldn’t figure out a way to stop the alarm after hitting “snooze” to silence the full-volume alarm sounds (so I could think strait without my brain oozing out my ears). 😵‍💫 I get that it’s meant to prevent us from just turning it off in our sleep, and help jog the brain awake, but there needs to be a, “I’m already awake, standing in my living room, and don’t feel like stopping mid-morning-routine to do your stupid puzzles,” button or something.

I turned off the chatbot, which was annoying, and I’m glad that option was available, but there need to be more ways to customize. And, I agree that that the lag times are perplexing. text: Versatility and SMART goals . This review is for the subscription version of the app. After a few days of trying it for free, I was hooked. I have never before rated an app voluntarily before being asked by the app. This app is amazing and has proven to be extraordinarily productive for me, especially as someone with diagnosed ADHD. For those who may not know, SMART goals = specific, measurable, achievable, realistic, and time-limited. This app is like the to-do list I always wanted. Not only does it allow me to set goals and objectives, it also gives me several ways of looking at my data. It keeps me on track and I’ve been able to see tangible results. The flexibility comes in because it allows you to play around with all aspects of the SMART goals. For example, I’m reminding myself to drink water because I usually don’t unless there’s coffee or tea in it. I’m keeping track of my weight with an ultimate weight goal that I’ve selected on the date that I’ve selected. I’m keeping track of the things I eat so that I can develop more healthy patterns of eating by setting goals. I’m completing a project at home that I’ve literally been neglecting for years. The app gives me information about how I’m doing after I set my parameters and report my progress. I’m keeping track of the professional reading I’m doing because I’m able to reinforce this behavior as well as other behaviors that I’m cultivating. You get the idea. The other thing that I like about this app, which may be a minor detail, is that it does not include “cute“ graphics. The app has all the graphics you need presented in a straightforward and readable manner. Finally, there are numerous predefined trackers under multiple categories, but you also have the option of creating your own. The only additional feature I can think of would be to be able to set a tracker that included a timer for doing a particular task; for example, doing something that you don’t like, but you know that you need to do, for 15 minutes or 30 minutes per day for that task with an alarm at the end. But that’s not a dealbreaker in anyway because I can already do that on the iPhone. Wait! One more thing: the developer also makes available tutorials on setting goals. This is what tipped me over the edge and made me come here to write this review. You will not regret subscribing to this app. The end and thank you!

text: One easy step away from being perfect . I am an adult with severe ADHD and struggle with staying on task throughout the day due to time blindness, distractions and horrible short term memory. I’ve downloaded and tried nearly every well reviewed calendar and planning app I can find and can easily say none of them compare to the clean, simple, customizable UI of this one. The constant start/end reminders, color coding, customization and live visual of how much time is left with each task are simple things that are life changing for someone with ADHD, and likely plenty of non-ADHDers. Seeing these options, I quickly subscribed to the annual year plan and started setting up daily systems to keep me on track. The one major flaw that is forcing me to continue with google calendar/tasks rather than this app is that there is no option to repeat tasks on specific days. For example, setting a task to repeat only on Tuesdays & Thursdays, M-F or only on one specific day of the week or repeat on a specific day of the month. My schedule varies throughout the week and I have drastically different schedule and routine on weekends. Being forced to manually input everything for every single weekday & every single weekend or having my weekday tasks repeat “everyday” is quite the shortfall. Daily manual input takes away the efficiency & automation of systematic routines & having weekday task reminders repeated on weekends, is quite the nuisance. If the option becomes available to select specific days of the week for reoccurring tasks, I will quickly edit this review to be 5-stars, recommend to everyone and switch to relying on this app for staying on track. I hope to see this update very soon because this app is otherwise incredible and I really want to put it to use. Having only one complaint, though it’s a bit of a make or break for me, the developers have done an amazing job with this planner. Keep it up.

LOVE THIS, but heads up for Beta users . I love this app so much. I have ADHD and struggle with being overwhelmed by too many calendars, adding tasks/reminders/to-do’s in different locations and then losing them. This app is amazing because it somehow pulls info from wherever I added it (apple reminders, all my calendars, all day events) and drills it down to what I need to do NEXT and what I need to do TODAY. 

I’m the kind of person who needs to put “take garbage out” on my calendar and this app simply and beautifully lets me know that I haven’t done it yet and strikes it out when I did (it’s fun to check off boxes when you did something too).

Great widgets (multiple size options), endless custom colors, and nice interface on the Apple Watch. I wish complications on the watch were a little more varied (being able to see your text task in text/word form instead of just an icon) but I can’t complain about it. It’s nice to flick my wrist and see right away that “call mom” is the next thing unchecked. I don’t have to search for it, it’s just there. 

I bought the full version of this app the second day I used it. It’s just so clean and modern looking. Not TOO many useless options to confuse my ADHD brain, but the options are there if you need/want them. If I had to search for criticisms I would say more/different watch complications would be helpful, and possibly customizable widgets for the phone/iPad. But that’s a stretch - this app is perfect now. 

**iOS 16 Beta**  Widgets do not work which is to be expected but the app still runs fine if you open it. Also does not work on the Beta for Apple Watch. I wish I knew before I committed to the beta testing because I would have honestly preferred the app widgets to work than to see what the new iOS was all about. Just for reference, none of my 3rd party apps are working great on the Beta so this is not an app problem at all. Just a caution to any nerds who want to get this app now but may want to try beta testing down the line.

app: 1. Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text:
Unfortunately, not ADHD friendly . I’m just letting this warning here because it was nowhere to be found before I purchased the app: they REMOVED THE “ROUTINE” FUNCTION in some update, despite promoting this feature in all of their communications. That said, this really doesn’t matter AS MUCH, since you can still create one activity called, let’s say… “Morning Routine” and have subtasks on it.

But as an ADHDer myself, this app has 2 flaws that I simply cannot understand, even more on an app that is made by and for us neurodivergents: 1) it “punishes” you if you are late for any activity 2) it does not allow to enter activities with a due date+time, but without a defined duration. Let me explain:

1)
ALL activities have an individual and automatic timer, that starts at the due date/time an it is great to be able to see the activity and the time passing by in real time WHEN YOU CAN MAKE IT ON TIME. Because if you, for some reason are late, you CANNOT STOP IT, or even edit it. Only pause it. Also, if you accidentally tap on the “play” button right above an activity, you cannot undo it. For both cases (activity already started or accidentally tap on “play” button), you have to delete the activity and re-insert it!

Let me give an example: I had a swimming class today on my Google Calendar at 10AM but the teacher couldn’t make it and just told me after 10AM. Tiimo has an integration with GC, so it imported the event, but right at 10pm the timer started to roll until 11am, automatically! You cannot edit ANY event, the imported and/or the ones we create originally in app, AFTER it starts.

I wrote an email about all I’m writing here, and they’ve confirmed: I have to DELETE the activity and re-insert it again, with the new date/time. And if the activity was imported from GC, I have to go out of the app, go to Google Calendar, delete and re-enter the event with the new date+time. That’s more time wasting and more opportunities to make mistakes and forget things…

2)
Another big flaw for me is that we cannot create activities/events without a defined duration. Let’s say I want to wash my dishes at 2PM, but I don’t know how much time it takes yet. We all know “time blindness” is a struggle for us with ADHD and Autism! But in this app, instead, I have to create an activity on the day I want and leave it as “any time of the day” option, and remember that I need to do it by 2PM myself. That’s right, a planning app in which you have to use your own memory (and we all know how bad our memories are, that’s why we look for apps in the first place)…

They give us another workaround, that is to create the “washing dishes” task with an approximate duration and DURING THE ACTIVITY, keep tapping the “+” icon to add more minutes. With my hands wet?! And if I was on my swimming class and it was longer than it usually is? I have to leave the pool running and go to the app to add more time before the class ends?

How frustrating it is, to set an arbitrary time for something, like “editing a video”, and have to pause the activity itself to get the phone and keep adding minutes? How distracting and disappointing it is?

So, basically, I need to pay for this app and for another one like Toggl to first track the time I take to do every single activity in my life and then use Tiimo. That doesn’t make sense.

And another consequence of this, is that I cannot have on the same app, my tasks/activities and basic reminders, like someone’s birthday or holiday! If you import a “moon phase” or any calendar I just mentioned to Tiimo that is just an reminder for the day (and not a task per se), you have to set a timing duration or it will be together with the “anytime” tasks during the day.

I just don’t understand… so now I have to pay for Tiimo, Toggl and have to leave the app and enter on my Calendar app to see “all day” events that aren’t tasks, like “credit card due date”, or “Easter”. That’s the perfect recipe for failure as someone who struggles with focus and attention!

_

So, to summarize, on Tiimo, I have the following results by the end of my day:

• A swimming lesson that I supposedly did, but in reality didn’t;

• A pile of dishes in the sink, that I now have to wash in the evening when I am out of energy and tired, because I couldn’t guess the duration, so the task went to the “anytime” tab, that was closed to avoid distractions from the main ones;

• A full afternoon supposedly without any activity,  because I needed to use another app to track the time I took to edit a video, so that I can add it more accurately on Tiimo the next time;

• Oh, and I forgot to call my friend on her birthday, because I couldn’t add this event on Tiimo without a task attached to it and didn’t entered my Calendar app today 

_
I know the creator’s intentions are good, so I don’t plan on lashing out here. I really have tried the workarounds, but all I did was waste my money and patience. I’ll be testing Tick-Tick now, since they have all the functions mentioned, a minimalist layout and widgets way more useful!

app: 1. Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text:
Heading in the wrong direction . I’m using Tiimo begrudgingly and out of desperation. 

On one hand, it’s the only app I’ve managed to find that offers the niche functions I need: task management, time blocking, live activities and Apple Watch complications, and focus timers that automatically start at scheduled times. It allows me to plan my day in advance and reduce the friction of having to make in-the-moment decisions the following day, which is a big help for folks with ADHD. I can easily see what I should be doing at any given moment and how long I have left to do it. So yeah—kudos to making my days a bit easier.

On the other hand, the Tiimo team seems to be going in a direction that many users, myself included, don’t actually want—any amount of online research will reveal similar sentiments.

1. It’s clear that they’re trying to force users to use their AI assistant. From any tab in the app (including the focus timer), the purple assistant icon stares at you, begging to be clicked. On top of the icon, you’ll sometimes see a banner in the Today tab when you open the app, prompting you to plan your day with the assistant. I don’t doubt that it might be useful for some users, but why not provide the option to hide/toggle it off or at least put it in its own tab? The extra UI clutter for a feature that should be discretionary and the fact that the team is so heavy-handed with their promotion of it isn’t very ADHD-friendly. 

2. The ability to create and save custom routines is unclear. From the Today view, you have the option to explore routines from your recent tasks (those with sub-task) or select one from a library of premade routines. However, there’s no guidance about what a routine actually is in the context of the app and how to actually create one in a way that’s modular and intuitive. Your best bet is creating a to-do item with sub-tasks and then having it repeat, choosing a preset, or asking the chat assistant to help you.

3. Their website (not the web app) seems to bombard you with popups to subscribe to Pro each time you navigate to a new page. Being a paid subscriber who sometimes wants to just browse their resource or product pages, the popups are already quite irritating. But for a potential user looking to spend money and commit to a new app, the frequent interruptions are pushy and distracting—two things that set off alarm bells for someone with ADHD.

I really want to like Tiimo and use it long-term, which is why I put all this effort into typing up my feedback in the first place. I can largely ignore or overlook most of the issues I have with the app, and I believe the Tiimo team generally does care about supporting people with ADHD. 

But the app’s lack of flexibility and choice when it comes to their AI tool is a red flag for me—it points to a possible business-driven desire to be competitive in the AI space which, at least in my case, comes at the expense of user agency, needs, and preferences. I’ll likely stick with Tiimo until something better comes along, but I’m pessimistic about the direction the app’s development will take.

app: 1. Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text:
An absolute lifesaver for those with learning differences . I don’t normally leave app reviews but if there’s one app that deserves it it’s Tiimo. Developing a routine and positive habits is a continuous challenge for me, and my as-yet-untreated ADHD has caused me to try almost every app on the App Store to organise myself. I somehow keep returning to Tiimo however, a year after I first signed up.

Firstly, Tiimo has an incredibly user friendly interface, and it feels pleasant to use. There are lots of different icons available to visually distinguish between activities and tasks. On the premium membership, importing your calendar events is seamless.

Several features really make Tiimo stand apart from other planning tools. Unlike just using Apple Calendar, for example, Tiimo has a timer view that allows you to only see what you’re working on right now. For someone like me that is prone to distraction this is critical. No other apps seem to implement this in the same way as Tiimo.

Another feature is that there are several different ‘levels’ available for your activities and tasks. For example, you could have a single activity as it’s own timer, or if you’re working on something that has lots of steps you can use checklists that sit below a particular activity. Activities themselves can be combined as part of routines that themselves can be saved, set to repeat and so on. 

I’ve found the most effective mornings I’ve had over the past year have been ones where I have all my morning activities laid out for me in advance and I can just move my way through the timers. Otherwise I never get anywhere!

As a final point, the app is specifically designed for folks with specific challenges, be this ASD, ADHD, and so on, and as such I find it fits my brain really well. Knowing that this user base is in mind in every step of the design process is fantastic, and I believe the team deserve all the credit for their hard work. They’re also incredibly open to suggestions and feedback, and the subscription price I feel is incredibly reasonable for an app that you can use every single day, all day long, for all manner of uses. It particularly shines when used in conjunction with a smart watch (e.g. the Apple Watch) as I can leave my phone somewhere else as I just follow the timers on my wrist.

I could keep going so I’ll stop here! Thank you for developing Tiimo - the community feels so supportive and positive and it’s brought a little bit of light into my life while I’ve been navigating receiving an ADHD diagnosis as an adult.

app: 86. Today Habit tracker - For to-dos, routines & goals
text:
Great tool for those with ADHD . The Today Habit Tracker app has been monumental for me as someone with severe ADHD. Being able to plan ahead and create daily and weekly routines, along with corresponding widgets, has made scheduling and planning daily life a breeze. The app is simple, elegant, and full of features. I have subscribed to a year of premium due to its benefits. However, I’ve noticed it lacks some critical functionality and contains a couple bugs. I’d love to see an update with some or all of the following addressed!
* When selecting “view/edit data” on a custom chart, the app crashes — there is no way to change, remove, or edit the number entered originally.
* Some health categories I am interested in displaying are missing — like medications taken/skipped
* Being able to launch shortcuts or apps within a habit could be a great feature to make completing tasks simpler. * I would love to be able to create a section for “bad habits” — most of what I use the app for is daily and weekly tasks like laundry, meds, and exercise. Having a section for bad habits, like arguing, vaping, drinking, etc. where I could keep track of these habits and focus on quitting them could be great.
* I would also love to see more integration with other third party apps, like Spotify (for quick launching playlists and choosing tunes for each habit), Calm/Headspace (for quickly starting a random or preselected meditation), Nike Run Club (for starting workouts quickly and seeing more detailed information), and possibly smart home apps — like HomeKit, Alexa, LG Thinq, or Tuya — setting routines from within the app and having access to information like washer/dryer time remaining would be monumental.
* The Pillow sleep tracking app, which is made by the same developer, isn’t integrated at all into this app — with sleeping habits being integral to a healthy lifestyle, I’d love to see more feature tie ins between the two.
* Milestones, which are essentially mini checklist widgets sitting below a habit, don’t automatically reset daily with no option to have the app do so. I use this feature for tasks such as my meditation routine, morning rituals, and logging medication I have taken on a specific day. Being able to choose to have these lists reset daily, as well as being able to see a history of what was checked off on what day and when, would go a long way for me.
* The Welzen meditation app, which is prominently featured on a widget, isn’t available in the U.S. app store — once the widget is added, it is functionally useless. I’d love to see a revamped mindfulness feature!
Overall, this app is a great tool for those who need it, and with some improvement, would be an instant purchase for me! As these bugs and missing features are addressed, I will definitely up my rating to 5 stars — this app is very close to being perfect!

For a person with ADD, this can be extremely damaging, as you may forget what you previously entered. Don’t rely on the app to save anything. Pen and paper are a better, more reliable fix!

It is also highly irritating that users cannot set a default for duration of tasks (everything is set to 30 minute increments). Users should be able to set this when they enter a task. 20 tasks? Now you have 20 edits and at least 20-40 crashes.

None of users “incompleted”tasks forward to future days. 

So, if you have ADHD and are potentially forgetful (we all are!) due to the bombardment of stimuli… No worries, you will NEVER be prompted to finish a task or to see a reminder “to do” that you enter.

Clunky and inefficient without any double-check.

No calendar options for planning tasks ahead of schedule (procrastinators will LOVE this lack of planning).

Tired of boring, mindane tasks? no worries… This app makes you enter the same information every single day. Do you need routine timers for staying on task, not losing your focus? Well, then this app is not for you. 

I spent about 20 minutes every morning (for 4-6 months) entering my to do list, editing the time needed per event and watching insane amounts of crashes. 

NOT A CALENDAR!
Tasks cannot be repeated. There is no calendar option. There is only today. 

Apparently there’s no need to plan forward or maybe look at the past week’s events, to repeat tasks or time routine tasks that are important (it’s not like people with ADHD get distracted throughout the day and throughout the mundane process of managing their priorities and time).😂

I find myself mindlessly re-entering the exact same information, day-after-day, (tell me why this is better than a manual daytimer???)

The app is supposed to help you get things done and be more efficient. 

I find it to be a time sink. 

TORTUROUS SOUNDS

And if I don’t finish a task that day, it’s easy to add it back into my schedule the next day. I can also see my progress on which tasks I’ve completed. So I can easily count up the hours spent on each project. 

I have a hard time estimating how long tasks take and by extending  the time block and moving a task to the next day, I’ve been realizing how much I under estimate my time projections. No wonder I always feel behind. 

It’s so easy to extend the time block for a task and move other tasks to a different time block. You can set up time blocks as small as 5 minutes. And you can drag over multiple tasks into one time block. 

I also want to add that the user interface is so simple and intuitive to use. It’s great not to feel overwhelmed by features. It also syncs across all Mac devices for the paid version. And there are notifications for each time block. You can test out so many features in the free version. I paid for the premium version to sync my calendar and use over all my devices. The developer also takes feedback of feature requests and improves the app with them. 

I feel in command of my work schedule now. Having ADHD and difficulty with time management and with trouble getting started on tasks because my todo list seems overwhelming, it’s been a life saver for me.

text:

I also need an alarm that continues to go off because it's very difficult for me to wake up in the morning. Instead of my alerts repeating indefinitely, or even more than a small handful of times (I just tested it and the 1 minute snooze repeated only 9 times before stopping, I lost the data on the 5 and 10 minute snooze settings, but I've set all of my alarms to 5 min snooze before this). What ends up happening is, for example, the alarm starts going off in the morning for me to wake up, but I don't hear it/consciously register it and then after just a few repeats, it's off completely. So I don't wake up on time, and then when I eventually do, the first thing I see is that the alert went off HOURS ago and stopped. EXTREMELY frustrating.

I opened the app today (with not even any pending task notification numbers displayed on the Due badge) at random, only because I'd thought to check it, and had a LONG list of alerts that were all permanently snoozed from as far back as 2 WEEKS AGO, and I was never able to mark them as "done." Because they just turned off on their own.

I need alerts to literally repeat until I am ready to turn them off manually. To compensate for this issue I've ended up making ~six different alerts for the same task that I can't afford to forget about at slightly different times. The calendar alert system on iOS only gives me limited options to forewarn me of an event, and once it alerts me once, it doesn't alert me again, and I have to remember to reset the alert as the event gets closer. I really need an app that can do this. This app would be great if the repeat function actually repeated more than a small, set number of times.

app: 49. Focus Keeper - Pomodoro Timer - ADHD Organizer & Productivity
text:
Helpful for ADD . I have never written a review before. However, this app has changed my life. I have ADD. When I tried to study before I  used this app, I had to spend an unsustainable amount of time to complete my work. This was because I was constantly getting distracted. Now, when I work, I always have my cell phone out on my desk with this app going. For me, distraction always starts with me looking up and around. Now, when I do that, I see this app’s “focus session” screen counting away. Then I remember that I am on “focus” time, and get back to my task. Also, knowing I have a guilt-free break coming up makes me not rebel against focusing for 25 minutes. The knowledge that I will have time to get important things done besides studying motivates me. 

I recommend getting the pro version. Being able to adjust the time for breaks is essential for me. I am a mother, so the things that I used to try to multitask, I now do one at a time during my breaks. Sometimes, I need more than 5 minutes to finish the dishes, etc. I can adjust the time of each break on the “break screen” with pro. It takes 2 seconds. Setting my chores, studying, etc up this way takes away the excuse that I had about needing to do chores or other important things instead of studying. 

Because this app prevents the screen from locking, it never disappears like the regular timer app on my phone. I don’t have to reset it each time a session ends either. It is all automatic. Resetting a timer over and over on my own would never have worked with my ADD. I don’t think I conveyed how much this app has changed my life. It is a night and day difference.

text:
Recommended by OT but not quite doing the job. . I have AUDHD with some OCD, anxiety and exhaustion. I am dealing with physical disability as well from nervous system and autoimmune issues. I’m in occupational therapy for speech, physical rehab, and soon will be adding visual OT. My speech therapist thinks that the root of a lot of my problems is actually exhaustion from excessive screen time. My screen time has become an escape hatch from my preexisting issues, but it worsens them so it’s an endless feedback loop. We are using this app to try stepping down from my usage of social media in particular. 


Most of us have multiple devices. I have an iPad, MacBook, iPhone and Apple Watch and the app doesn’t automatically sync across these devices. It doesn’t automatically lock down all my devices, I have to grow a tree separately on each even after syncing them. 

It doesn’t reliably block access to apps when in focus mode. It says I’m in focus right now and I can access all my apps without killing my tree. 

I don’t like the stats board. I have premium and it is showing me whatever I’ve tagged my usage as, instead of using existing Apple analytics to populate that chart. Rocket money and Mint seem to be able to create good pie charts and graphs based off access to account info, so wondering why this isn’t the same. 

I find the current description key for the charts comparing one day against another a bit vague. More concise wording is needed to provide a key to understanding that one. Is this even a helpful metric? Why not something more simple and engaging like “wow, you did it! Your break from screens lasted 20% longer than yesterday, with a total of 4.5 hours!” The way it’s set up now is very flat and boring and tbh hard to tell if it’s a positive or negative comparison. 

The daily challenge always has one goal I can’t meet without cashing in all my coins on a plant I don’t have to unlock it. Not a fan of that as a premium user. 

I did like being able to set focus to run from a set time in morning to a set time in evening. I didn’t like that it doesn’t automatically remember this setting and do it every day Monday through Friday (or whatever you prefer). It did it well for my first day, and then wasn’t in place the next morning. I really need the features to run for consecutive days in order for this to work. Relying on me to remember or have the willpower to do this every day in the beginning is not helpful. I have adhd, this is not accounting for how our disability shows up. We are more prone to addiction to screens, and have more difficulty creating new habits, especially when the new habit is in conflict with an established maladaptive ritual. A setting where I can explain what level assistance I need, and then consent to a time frame or schedule for the week/month would work better than what it’s doing now. 


I’d love to see a journal of symptoms and encouragement/coping strategies  included in the app. Other addiction apps provide structured support for the hard parts of cycle breaking. Since I’m doing this on the recommendation of a doctor, would be cool to be able to log symptoms and share that kind of chart with them over time. To view my progress that way. 
For example, I experienced a lot of anxiety and agitation my first day. I had observations about my energy levels, and would like to have stored what I did with my time instead on the app for a productivity chart or something. I also experienced insomnia my first night, and would have benefitted from charting that, sleep as a metric is useful, and possibly links to resources to help fall asleep. 


I hate the “take a break” options. The breathing animation and “peaceful sounds” are awful. They’re loud and distracting, and without sound pretty useless. The breathing is way too fast for calming down. 

And last, I much prefer setting up the app to block my access to specific things for a set time period, vs checking it every 20 minutes or so to get a tree. Why cant we still get trees and coins for the time we are in deep focus for hours? I get ONE tree no matter how long the break is. Repeatedly checking the app is defeating the purpose of staying off the device. Picking it up to do that makes me want to check social media. I’m trying to wean off the default of looking at my phone during my more functional hours when I should be doing IRL things.

text:

However, after this recent update, I’ve really struggled to use it. They changed the font, the way tasks are added, and how things are displayed. While I understand they’ve added many new features that might be helpful to others, they seem to have completely overlooked the user experience. 

This is an app specifically designed for people who dislike sudden changes or struggle with complex steps, yet this update introduced so many new elements, steps, and design changes. It’s no longer a helpful tool for me; instead, it has become a source of frustration. Unfortunately, I won’t be renewing my subscription.

app: 1. Tiimo- To-Do List Planner - Schedule Structured Daily Task
text:
Beautiful design, but frustrating to use . I’ve had a Tiimo subscription for two years, and I genuinely like the design and visual approach of the app. Unfortunately, I keep running into the same problem: there’s so much friction involved in creating, editing, and rescheduling tasks that I eventually stop using it after a few weeks.

Ironically, for me, it’s one of the least ADHD-friendly planners I’ve tried. A planner should reduce the mental effort required to organize my day, not become another task I have to manage.

I’ve also given the AI assistant several chances, but so far it’s been more of a waste of time than a helpful feature. For example, I gave it a simple instruction to schedule my work shifts for next week, from 16:00 to midnight, with Tuesday and Thursday off. It initially scheduled me for all seven days, and I had to repeatedly clarify the instructions and specify exact dates to prevent it from changing other weeks.

By the time the AI finally understands what I want, I’ve spent more time explaining and correcting it than it would have taken to enter everything manually.

I really want to love Tiimo because the visual design is excellent. But the functionality needs to be much more intuitive, flexible, and reliable. For an ADHD planner, reducing friction should be the number one priority.

text:
Great for neurodivergence/fatigue . I have ADHD and fatigue from long Covid. The ability to track the energy that tasks drain and set an energy budget for each day is unique to Structured, I think, and over the last few days it's been helping me turn my life around (and that's not ADHD exaggeration!). What's really helped is the recognition that, with ADHD, if I don't set aside specific time for a task, then I'm unlikely to be able to do it. So Structured has started to feel like critical assistive technology for me.

It's close to perfect. Even though it doesn't have full calendar integration, it makes it very easy to edit Apple Calendar events through a modal, so no problems with that. I've given it 4/5 rather than 5/5 for these things which I hope will be improved:

• I can't adjust the length of events with touch-drag, only their start-time. There needs to be the ability to long-press near the end of an event bar to adjust its time.
• I'd like a settings option to say that when I'm touch-dragging events around, the adjustment will snap to increments of 5 minutes (or 15 mintes, or 1 minute (for the weirdos who like to set events with 1-minute accuracy!)).
• For a task system, there needs to be additional categories than just "Inbox" in which to store tasks, eg with "folders" or similar. Without this, I need to keep using an external tool to track tasks for projects, then copy them into Structured in some way when they need to get done.

The overly-precise event dragging and lack of drag/drop event length I decided I could live with.

The lack of task folders for non-scheduled tasks means I need an external tool for my projects (I'm using Obsidian, but Todoist is great too), but Structured's time-line and energy tracking has such value that it's worth it for me to have an extra app in my process. Also, in honesty, the limitation of having only an inbox for non-scheduled tasks is interesting in a positive way. It's helping me to not overthink day-to-day planning, because overthinking/overcomplexity is a mostly harmful tedency I have. So when Structured implements task folders (which I hope they do), I'll try to keep hold of what this limitation is teaching me and not overcomplicate my folders and bury things.

Definitely recommend you take a look if you have fatigue/pacing challenges. I think it's fantastic value, especially on a yearly plan.

app: 2. Structured- Daily Planner Todo - Visual Calendar & Organizer
text:
This app deserves 5 Stars… but it needs a few more features. . I downloaded this app yesterday, and it is fantastic. I have ADHD, and being able to put all my to dos and calendars and routine items into one place, viewable on a calendar with checkboxes to tick them off, is AMAZING. Easily worth the annual subscription for the pro version to open up all the features. 

But it needs just a few more:

1) I’d love to see the ability to change the time of multiple events on a given day at the same time: I’m thinking of this as a “edit my day” button that allows selection of multiple events, moving them all together earlier or later in the day. 

2) It would be super helpful to have the ability to reorganize subtasks. I don’t always think of subtasks in order and having them out of order really messes with my head. So I have more than once added in the new subtask I need and then copy and pasted each following subtask below. It’s a unnecessarily cumbersome process. From what I can tell, this could be solved in two possible ways: allow the cursor to create a new subtask when the return key is pushed or the “new subtask” button pressed even if there is a subtask already below, or provide mover bars on each subtask to be able to freely move them within the list. 

3) The icing on the cake would be an option to allow overlapping events when they are 4+ hours long. Maybe a checkbox in the event? This would ideally allow it to stretch beneath other events on the day’s view to help get a feel for what things are overlapping and when to see if they can be worked in or need to be moved. 

Thank you for a great app, and I hope improvements can be made to make it that much better!

app: 2. Structured- Daily Planner Todo - Visual Calendar & Organizer
text:
Amazing! But I need a little more . As a person with ADHD, I have a really hard time adhering my my to do list without a structured plan for WHEN to do the tasks. I also have a difficult time determining how long tasks actually take, so I plan 30 to-dos, thinking that I can accomplish them all, and feel bad about myself when I fail to do so. I’ve tried the time blocking method on my Google Calendar, but I’ve always had trouble sticking to it. 

If you struggle with the same issues, this app is worth checking out!

It is essentially a time-blocking app that integrates your to-dos. What sets this app apart from using Google Calendar and a to-do list is that it shows how far along you are in a specific task/event. It also is extremely visually appealing. It is much easier to use for time-blocking than Google Cal and it just makes more sense for my brain. The widgets are also helpful and beautifully designed.

For only $10, you can integrate your Apple calendar and Apple Reminders app to directly import your events and to-do’s. For a 1 time $10 fee, this is so worth it. Especially because you will have access to the premium features on all of your Apple devices.

The reason why I am giving this app 4 stars instead of 5 is because I can’t actually use it for my needs. I personally use Things 3 as a my task manager and I love it (even though I hardly get everything done because of my time-blindness, lol). I tried moving everything over to Apple Reminders, but I just can’t use it as my primary task manager. I could move what I NEED to do right now over to Apple Reminders, but its just too much work and would take away too much time from actually getting things done.

I also wish that I could directly connect my Google Calendar to the app. I worked around this by integrating my Google Cal with Apple Cal, so that my events import. But if I make any changes to my Google Cal, it takes FOREVER for the change to update on Structured.

If you use Reminders and Apple Cal, this app is incredible. I highly recommend it to anyone, honestly. But I really really really wish that I could use this directly with Things 3. There are probably other people who would like to use this with other apps like Todoist as well. 

I know that this app is developed by one person which is very impressive because it is so amazing and functional. So I also know that is probably really hard for one person to create an integration with Things 3 and other apps. Fingers crossed that this can happen someday 🤞 until then, I can only admire this app from afar 🥺
